```{r setup}
library(symcompR)
x <- Symbol("x"); y <- Symbol("y"); z <- Symbol("z")
a <- Symbol("a"); b <- Symbol("b"); p <- Symbol("p"); q <- Symbol("q")
f <- Function("f"); g <- Function("g")
```

This vignette covers pattern matching with wildcards, `sympy.unify`,
`sympy.strategies`, and the expression paths of
`sympy.simplify.epathtools`.

## Pattern matching

`Wild()` creates a pattern variable. `sym_match()` returns the values of the
wildcards for which the pattern equals the expression, or `NULL` when there
are none. The `exclude` argument keeps a wildcard from matching expressions
containing given symbols.

```{r}
wa <- Wild("a", exclude = list(x)); wb <- Wild("b", exclude = list(x))
sym_match(3 * x + 2, wa * x + wb)
sym_match(x^2 + 5, wa * x + wb)
```

`sym_replace()` replaces every match of a pattern:

```{r}
u <- Wild("u")
sym_replace(sin(x)^2 + 1, sin(u), cos(u))
sym_replace(f(x) + f(y), f(u), g(u))
```

`WildFunction()` matches any function application:

```{r}
F <- WildFunction("F")
sym_match(f(x), F)
sym_match(x + cos(x), x + F)
```

## Unification

`unify()` finds all ways to make two expressions equal by assigning the given
variables, taking commutativity into account.

```{r}
unify(a + b, x + y, variables = list(x, y))
```

`rewriterule()` turns a pattern and a replacement into a rule, which
returns all the rewritten forms. A condition can restrict the matches.

```{r}
rewriterule(p^2, p^3, variables = list(p))(x^2)
rewriterule(p^2 + q^3, (p * q)^4, list(p, q))(x^2 + y^3)
rewriterule(x, x + 1, list(x), function(x) isTRUE(x < 10))(Integer(5))
rewriterule(x, x + 1, list(x), function(x) isTRUE(x < 10))(Integer(15))
```

The unification engine works on generic trees. `unify_compound()` builds a
node from an operator and arguments, `unify_variable()` a variable, and
`unify_condvariable()` a variable with a condition. `unify_core()` returns
all the substitutions that unify two trees.

```{r}
v <- unify_variable("v")
t1 <- unify_compound("Add", list(1, 2))
t2 <- unify_compound("Add", list(v, 2))
unify_core(t1, t2)
cv <- unify_condvariable("w", function(e) e > 1)
unify_core(t1, unify_compound("Add", list(1, cv)))
unify_core(t1, unify_compound("Add", list(cv, 2)))
```

## Rewriting with strategies

`sympy.strategies` provides combinators for building rewrite systems out of
simple rules. A rule is a function from an expression to an expression;
`exhaust()` applies a rule until nothing changes, `chain()` applies rules in
sequence, and `greedy()` explores a tree of alternatives and keeps the best
result by an objective function.

```{r}
inc <- function(e) if (isTRUE(is_integer(e)) && as.numeric(e) < 5) e + 1 else e
exhaust(inc)(Integer(1))
chain(inc, inc)(Integer(0))
best <- greedy(list(function(e) expand(e), function(e) sym_factor(e)),
               objective = count_ops)
best(x^2 + 2 * x + 1)
```

### Rules

A rule takes an expression and returns a new one. The rules of
`sympy.strategies.rl` work on any node; `strat_new()` builds one with a
given operator, here a generic `Basic` node.

```{r}
B <- function(...) strat_new(list(type = "Basic"), ...)
e <- B(S(1), S(0), S(2))
e
rm_id(function(a) a == 0)(e)
unpack(B(S(2)))
rl$flatten(B(S(1), B(S(2), S(3))))
rl$sort(function(a) as.numeric(a))(B(S(3), S(1), S(2)))
glom(function(a) a, function(a) 1, function(cnt, a) cnt * a)(B(S(2), S(2), S(3)))
distribute("Mul", "Add")(strat_new(list(type = "Mul"), S(2), strat_new(list(type = "Add"), x, y)))
rebuild(strat_new(list(type = "Add"), x, x))
rl$subs(S(1), S(5))(S(1))
```

`basic_fns` and `expr_fns` tell the traversals how to take a node apart and
put it back together; `expr_fns` evaluates the rebuilt expression.

```{r}
names(basic_fns)
traverse$top_down(function(e) if (isTRUE(e == 1)) S(9) else e)(B(S(1), B(S(1), S(2))))
traverse$bottom_up(function(e) if (isTRUE(is_integer(e))) e + 1 else e)(B(S(1), S(2)))
traverse$top_down(function(e) if (isTRUE(e == 1)) S(9) else e, fns = expr_fns)(x + 1)
```

### Combinators

`condition()` applies a rule only when a predicate holds, `do_one()` applies
the first rule that changes the expression, `minimize()` keeps the best of
several results, `strat_switch()` dispatches on a key, `typed()` dispatches
on the type of the expression, `memoize()` caches
results, `null_safe()` and `tryit()` return the input when a rule fails, and
`canon()` applies rules everywhere until nothing changes.
`strat_identity()` is the rule that does nothing, and `strat_debug()`
prints each step.

```{r}
inc <- function(e) e + 1; dec <- function(e) e - 1; dbl <- function(e) 2 * e
condition(function(e) e > 2, inc)(S(1))
do_one(strat_identity, inc)(S(1))
minimize(inc, dec, objective = as.numeric)(S(3))
strat_switch(function(e) e$type, list(Integer = inc))(S(1))
by_type <- typed(list(Integer = inc, Symbol = dbl))
vapply(lapply(list(S(3), x, x + 1), by_type), sstr, "")
memoize(inc)(S(1))
null_safe(function(e) NULL)(S(1))
tryit(function(e) stop("no"))(S(1))
canon(function(e) if (identical(e$type, "Basic") && length(e$args) == 1) e$args[[1]] else e)(B(B(S(1))))
strat_identity(x)
strat_debug(inc)(S(1))
```

### Trees of strategies

A list of rules is a choice and `strat_seq()` a sequence. `greedy()` takes
the best choice at each step, `brute()` tries all of them, and
`allresults()` returns every result. `treeapply()` evaluates a tree with
given functions for choices and sequences, and `branch` holds the branching
versions of the combinators, which return lists of results.

```{r}
tree <- list(inc, strat_seq(dec, dbl))
greedy(tree, objective = as.numeric)(S(4))
greedy(tree, objective = as.numeric)(S(1))
brute(tree, objective = as.numeric)(S(4))
allresults(tree)(S(4))
treeapply(list(strat_seq(3, 2), strat_seq(4, 1)), list(list = max, seq = min))
branch$multiplex(function(e) list(e + 1), function(e) list(e - 1))(S(3))
```

## Expression paths

`epath()` selects or modifies parts of an expression with a path language
similar to XPath: `/*` descends into all arguments, `/Name` filters by
class, and `/[i]` selects by position. `EPath()` stores a compiled path.

```{r}
EPath("/*/[0]")
e <- Symbol("t") + sin(x + 1) + cos(x + y + sym_E)
epath("/*/*/Symbol", e)
epath("/*/*/Symbol", e, function(s) 2 * s)
nested <- list(list(list(x, 1), 2), list(list(3, y), z))
epath("/*/[0]/Symbol", nested)
epath("/*/[-1]", nested)
```
